chunks: And from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ishaq ibn Ghalib, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, in one of his speeches where he mentioned the state of the Imams and their attributes, saying:

Indeed, Allah the Almighty has clarified His religion through the guiding Imams of the Prophet's family, and made His path clear through them, and opened for them the inner springs of His knowledge. So whoever from the nation of Muhammad knows the obligatory right of his Imam will taste the sweetness of his faith and know the virtue of the comeliness of his Islam.

Because Allah the Almighty appointed the Imam as a standard for His creation and made him an authority over those who obey Him. Allah clothed him with the crown of dignity and covered him with the light of the Almighty. He extends a connection to the sky, and his sustenance does not cease from him. And nothing of what is with Allah is attained except through the means of his connection, and Allah does not accept the deeds of the servants except through knowledge of him.

He is aware of what comes to him from the ambiguous problems of the night, the obscure issues of the paths, and the confusing trials. Allah the Almighty has continuously chosen them for His creation from the descendants of al-Husayn, from the progeny of each Imam. He selects them, chooses them, is pleased with them for His creation, and accepts them for Himself. Whenever an Imam from them passed away, Allah appointed for His creation an Imam who is a clear standard, a guiding light, and a standing authority and knowledgeable proof.

Imams from Allah who guide with the truth and judge by it. They are Allah's proofs, His callers, and His guardians over His creation. The servants follow their guidance, the lands are refreshed by their light, and the offspring grow by their blessings. Allah made them life for the beings, lamps for the darkness, keys for speech, and pillars for Islam. Thus, Allah's decrees ran through them according to their inevitable conclusion.

The Imam is the selected, the accepted, the guided, the chosen, and the expected one. Allah chose him for this and fashioned him with His eye in the dust when He created him, and in the world when He formed him as a shadow before creating him as a soul at the right side of His Throne. He is beloved with wisdom in the knowledge of the unseen with Him. He chose him by His knowledge and selected him for his purity as a remnant of Adam, a choice from the progeny of Noah, a chosen one from the family of Abraham, a lineage from Ishmael, and a purest from the household of Muhammad.

He has continuously been watched by the eye of Allah, protected by His angels. Repelled from him are the evils of the darkness and the breath of every sinner. Turned away from him are the evils of bad deeds. He is free from defects, hidden from disasters, infallible from slips, preserved from all obscenities. He is known for patience and piety in his youth, attributed to chastity, knowledge, and virtue when he matures. The affair of his father is entrusted to him, and he remains silent in speech during his father's lifetime.

When the term of his father ends and Allah's decree brings him to his will, and the will comes from Allah towards his love, and he reaches the end of his father's term and passes away, Allah's command becomes his after him. Allah entrusts him with His religion, makes him the proof over His servants, and a standing authority in His land. He strengthens him with His spirit, gives him His knowledge, deposits His secret with him, and appoints him for the great affair. He informs him of the clear explanation of his knowledge, appoints him as a standard for His creation, makes him a proof for the people of his world, a light for the people of his religion, and the one in charge of His servants.

Allah is pleased with him as their Imam. He entrusted him with His knowledge, hid His wisdom in him, and made him a guardian for His religion. He revives through him the paths of his way, its obligations, and its limits. He stands with justice when the people of ignorance are confused and confutes the people of debate with the shining light and the reaching cure, with the clear truth and the evident explanation from every exit, upon the path that the truthful from his fathers followed.
So no one ignores the right of this scholar except the wretched, no one denies him except the deviant, and no one leaves him except the one who opposes Allah.
ai.seo_question: What are the attributes and divine rights of the Imams according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (as) elaborates on the theological status of the Imams as divinely appointed guides and proofs for humanity, emphasizing their selection from the progeny of the Prophet and their infallibility. It describes their preservation by Allah, their role in transmitting knowledge and establishing justice, and concludes that recognition of the Imam is essential for the acceptance of deeds. The text specifically highlights the lineage from the progeny of Husayn (as), reinforcing the Shia doctrine of Imamate being restricted to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (7) Muhammad bin Yahya narrated from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Eessa from al-Hasan bin Mahboob from Iss’haq bin Ghalib that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said in one of his speeches when describing the imams:

“Allah the Almighty has declared his religion with the guiding imams of the Prophet’s family (as). He has shone His divine method with them and has uncovered to them the hidden springs of His knowledge. Whoever of Muhammad’s nation knows the right of his imam will taste the sweetness of his faith and find the virtue of the comeliness of his religion.

Allah has appointed the imam as a sign to His people and has made him the authority over the believers. Allah has put on the imam’s head the crown of gravity and has shed upon him some of His light. He is the means between the Heaven and people. Nothing of the blessings of Allah is gained except by the means of the imam. Allah does not accept the deeds of His people without regarding (the right of) their imam.

The imam is able to answer all the vague problems and is aware of all the ambiguous issues of the Sharia and the confusing questions of religion. Allah has chosen for His people the infallible imams from the descendants of al-Husayn (as) one after the other. He has been pleased with them and He has accepted them for His people. Whenever an imam goes to the better world, Allah appoints another as a guiding imam and a knowing authority to guide the people to the straight path of the truth.

The imams are the authorities of Allah, His preachers and guardians, by whom people are guided and nations are refreshed. Allah has made them as the means of life for His people, as the light in darkness and as the pillars of Islam. All that has been determined by the will of Allah.

The imams are the preferred choice of Allah, the chosen guides and expected deliverances. Allah has chosen them since the first creation. He has created them as shadows before making them as beings at the right side of His Throne with His care. He has endowed them with wisdom while in the unseen world near Him. He has created them as the pure remainder of Adam, the best of Noah’s progeny, the choice of Abraham’s family, the offspring of Ishmael and the purest progeny of Muhammad (as).

They are still under the care of Allah and they are protected by His angels. They are protected from the evil darkness and the evil of every devil. They are freed from handicaps and diseases. They are infallible before all kinds of obscenities. They are endowed with piety and patience. They are granted with abstinence, knowledge and virtue. An imam is entrusted with the position of his father. He keeps silent during the lifetime of his father.

But when the will of Allah determines to bring the father to the better world, the son becomes ready to receive the order of Allah. Allah will entrust the son after the death of the father with His religion and make him the authority over His people and the guardian on His earth. He assists him with His angels, grants him His knowledge, entrusts him with His secret, deputes him to undertake the great task, appoints him as the authority over His people, makes him as a light for the believers of His religion and entrusts him with their affairs.

Allah is pleased with him as His guardian over His people. He entrusts him with His knowledge, wisdom and religion. He makes him revive His path, obligations and penalties. In his turn, the imam spreads justice when the ignorant become confused, confutes the arguers with the clear proofs and the bright truth of his truthful fathers (as).
No one ignores this truth save the wretched, no one denies it save the deviate and no one leaves it aside save the opponents of Allah.”
